examples.en: My house is bigger than yours.

examples.sr: Он је виши [не̏го што̏] сам мислио.
examples.en: He is taller than I thought.

related.en: than — comparing nouns and pronouns: «већа од твоје», «паметнији од мене»
than — comparing actions, states, parts of a sentence: «боље је учити него губити време»

note: With numerals only од: ви̏ше̄ од де̏сет. Tip: «than» between two nouns is од, between two actions it is не̏го.

related.en: strong, hard — having strength and intensity
powerful, mighty — a display of strength: an action, a machine, will

note:
Typical combinations:
• ја̑к чо̏век, јака кафа, ја̑к ве̏тар
• сна́жан у̀дарац, сна́жан мо̀то̄р, снажна воља

examples.sr: На крају састанка прешли смо на [ра̀зно].
examples.en: At the end of the meeting we moved on to any other business.

related.en: miscellaneous, various — a set of unrelated things; the agenda item «any other business»
differently — unlike things are compared
varied, diverse — a wealth of kinds, forms, flavors

note: Close in meaning to разнолико: разно̀врстан, шаро̀лик.

related.en: this (demonstrative pronoun) — declines: «ова банка», «ово питање»
here is, here comes (particle) — does not decline; the thing named goes in the genitive

note: With е̏во the short pronoun forms are used: е̏во ме, е̏во га - «here I am», «here he is».

examples.sr: Запамтио сам сваку [ре̑ч] из ове песме.
examples.en: I memorized every word of this song.
This letter is hard to write.

examples.sr: Његов [го̏во̄р] на конференцији био је инспиративан.
examples.en: His speech at the conference was inspiring.

related.en: word — a single word of a language: «тачна реч»
letter — a sign of the alphabet
speech, dialect — a talk, a manner of speaking, a local dialect

note: Do not mix them up: сло̏во is a letter of the alphabet, and the word for «word» is ре̑ч.

related.en: life — not a part of the body
stomach, belly — where it hurts after a meal

note: «My stomach hurts» is боли ме стомак. The outer belly, the paunch, is тр̀бух.

examples.en: Look at the other side of the paper.

related.en: country, land — a territory; also soil and the planet
state, country — a political unit
side, page — the side of something, or a page of a book

note: «Country» is зѐмља or др̀жава; стра́на means «side» or «page».

meanings: драго ми је or задовољан сам?

examples.sr: [Дра̑го ми је] што си добио посао!
examples.en: I'm glad you got the job!

related.en: I'm satisfied — lasting satisfaction: with a job, a grade, a result
I'm glad, I'm pleased — a reaction to news or an event; with «да» or «што»

note: Дра̑го ми је also means «nice to meet you». A woman says задовољна сам.

related.en: to say, to tell — a short, specific statement; perfective
to say, to tell — the same as «рећи», but it has a present tense: «кажем»
to speak, to talk — the process of speaking, giving a speech, knowing a language
to tell, to chat — informal conversation

note: Ре̏ћи has no present tense: кажем is used instead. «To tell (a story)» is испри́чати.

examples.sr: Београд ми је [до̏м] већ десет година.
examples.en: Belgrade has been my home for ten years now.
We bought a house and two apartments.

examples.sr: Живим у малом [ста̑ну] на петом спрату.
examples.en: I live in a small apartment on the fifth floor.

related.en: home, hearth, homeland — a broader and warmer notion
house — a specific building
apartment, flat — a dwelling in an apartment building

note: До̏м also means an institution: дом здравља is a «health center», дом за старе a «nursing home». «At home» is код куће.

examples.en: He took a full handful of walnuts.

related.en: arm, hand — the whole arm from shoulder to fingers; the general word
hand, handful — only the hand itself; also a measure, a handful

note: «To shake hands» is ру̏ковати се.

examples.en: I don't know how to explain it.
She is as beautiful as an angel.

related.en: how, in what way — in questions and after verbs of speech and perception
like (comparison), as (a role) — comparison, a role, a profession

note: With да it means «as if»: као да спава. And ка̏ко after «see» or «hear» introduces a clause: чуо сам како пева.

meanings: умрети, преминути, упокојити се, угинути or цркнути?

examples.en: He died after a long illness.
A well-known actor passed away yesterday.
The Patriarch passed away at the age of ninety.
The dog died of old age.

related.en: to die — neutral, of people
to pass away — official: news, obituaries
to pass away, to repose — church style
to die, to perish — of animals
to croak, to kick the bucket — rude; jokingly of gadgets

note: Said of a person, цр̏кнути sounds like an insult, and у̀гинути as if the person were an animal.

examples.en: Turn on the light, it's dark.
Plug the phone into the charger.

related.en: to turn on, to light — to start up: a light, a TV, an engine
to plug in, to include — into a network, a discussion

note: The opposites: уга́сити is the opposite of упа́лити, искљу́чити of укљу́чити.

related.en: to want — a momentary wish, a decision
to wish, to want — softer and more polite, a longer-lasting wish

note: The short forms ћу, ћеш, ће come from хте̏ти and form the future tense: ја̑ ћу до́ћи.

examples.sr: Он је [јѐдӣнӣ] који је дошао на састанак.
examples.en: He is the only one who came to the meeting.
This car has a unique design.

related.en: only, sole — numerical exclusivity: one among many
unique — a quality: like nothing else, one of a kind

note: Једѝнствен also means «unified»: једѝнствено тр̏жӣште is a «single market».

examples.en: A cold juice is just what I need in this heat.

related.en: to like — taste and sympathy: «свиђа ми се песма», «свиђаш ми се»
to be pleasant, to do good — effect and well-being: «чај ми прија»

note: From прѝјати comes при̏ја̄тно! - «enjoy your meal». With both verbs the person who likes stands in the dative: ми, ти, му.

related.en: all, the whole (the entire body of things) — all the elements, the whole mass: «сав народ», «сва деца»
whole, entire, intact — wholeness or a full period: «читав дан», «читава књига»
whole, entire — a close synonym of «читав», common in speech: «цео град»

note: «Everyone» of people is сви̏, «everything» of things is све̏: сви су дошли, све је у реду.

related.en: to go — the basic verb of motion, on foot or by vehicle
to come, to arrive (impf. / pf.)
to leave, to go away (impf. / pf.)

note: До̀лазити and о̀длазити are imperfective, до́ћи and оти́ћи perfective: долазим сваке суботе, but дошао сам јуче.

examples.en: She is sitting alone in the room.

related.en: alone, by oneself (сама, само, сами); also «I am», from «бити»
only, just — does not change

note: A trap: са̏мо is also the neuter of сам: де́те је са̏мо - «the child is alone».

related.en: very — bookish: writing, news, formal style
very, a lot — the universal word in speech
really, just — emotion, sincerity, surprise

note: With a noun мно̏го requires the genitive: мно̏го љу̑ди. Ба̏ш adds emotion: ба̏ш је хла́дно - «it's really cold!»

related.en: again — neutral: something happened once more
once more, again — to repeat the same action
anew, from scratch — a new start

note: If in doubt, use о̏пе̄т: it fits almost always.

examples.en: He is taller than you think.

related.en: already; but, rather (after a negation): «не ја, већ он»
than; but, rather (after a negation): a comparison and «not A but B»

note: In «not A but B» both work: нѝје о̑н, ве̏ћ ја̑ = нѝје о̑н, не̏го ја̑. In a comparison «than» is only не̏го.

related.en: just now; not until — about time: «тек сам стигао»
only, just — a limit on quantity
barely, hardly, with difficulty

note: Једва чекам - «I can't wait». Те̏к у де̏вет - «not until nine».

examples.en: The driver was injured in the accident.

related.en: injured, hurt — only of people: a physical or emotional wound
damaged — of things, when it is unclear how
broken, spoiled — not working, food gone bad; also of corrupt people

note: Verbs: ра̀збити - to smash, сло̀мити - to break, напу̀кнути - to crack.

meanings: спавати, заспати, одспавати, наспавати се or преспавати?

examples.en: The baby is sleeping in the stroller.
I'm going to take a half-hour nap.
I slept through the whole day.

related.en: to sleep — the process of sleeping (impf.)
to fall asleep — the moment of dozing off
to take a nap, to sleep a little
to get enough sleep — to sleep your fill
to oversleep (a stretch of time); to sleep over

note: Преспа́вати also means «to stay the night»: можеш да преспаваш код нас - «you can stay the night at our place».

examples.en: He will probably arrive on time.
I hope the rain stops by evening.

related.en: maybe, perhaps — the chances are about even; neutral, any style
probably, most likely — high chances
I suppose, hopefully — colloquial, with hope or doubt

note: Ва̀љда often expresses hope: Ва̀љда ће би̏ти бо̏ље̄ - «hopefully it will get better».

examples.en: A buddy from school called me.
He is just an acquaintance to me.
He has been my mate since childhood.

related.en: friend, close friend — the closest circle
buddy, pal, comrade — a good acquaintance who may become a пријатељ
acquaintance
mate, buddy — a colloquial, warm word for a close friend

note: A group of friends is дру́штво or еки́па. «To become friends» is спријатѐљити се.

examples.en: It was a completely different movie.

related.en: other, another — a different thing or person, a choice among several
differently, otherwise (adv.) — the manner of an action
different (adj.) — different in quality

note: Дру̏гӣ also means «second» in order: дру̏гӣ пу̑т - «the second time».

related.en: oh, oops — soft and human: surprise, sympathy, embarrassment
ow, oh — sharp: pain, fear, shock
oh dear, woe — drama, panic, often ironic
phew, ugh — tiredness, relief, a sigh

note: The meaning depends a lot on intonation. A ready phrase: ку̏кӯ мѐнӣ! - «woe is me!»

examples.en: Many cultures exist in the world.
I want to become a doctor.

related.en: to exist, to be — there is, there exists
to become, to turn into — a change of state or profession

note: По̀стати is perfective, its imperfective is по̀стајати. Посто̀јати exists only as an imperfective.

examples.sr: Хоћеш ли да идемо [о̀на̄мо], код реке?
examples.en: Do you want us to go over there, to the river?
Go that way, the exit is there.

related.en: here, this way — direction toward the speaker
there, over there — toward a distant place
that way — along a familiar route
that way over there — a distant route off to the side

note:
Ту̀да̄ means «that way», not «to there»; «to there» is о̀на̄мо or та̏мо.

Three questions:
• о́вде, та̏мо - «where?»
• о̀ва̄мо, о̀на̄мо - «to where?»
• о̀вуда, ту̀да̄, о̀нуда - «by which way?»

examples.en: At least half a kilogram of meat is needed.
At least twenty people are coming to the party.
At least come for a coffee.
Drop by for at least half an hour.

related.en: at least, a minimum of — an exact quantity: «минимум пола килограма»
at least — of a number of people or things
at least — if nothing more: «бар повтори лекцију»
at least, even if — a concession: «сврати макар на пола сата»

note: Ма̀кар also means «even if»: ма̀кар и ка̏сно - «even if late».

examples.sr: Желим да се [извѝним] што сам закаснио.
examples.en: I want to apologize for being late.
The river wound through the valley.

related.en: to apologize — to ask for forgiveness
to bend, to wind — of objects: a tree, a river, a branch

note: Even native speakers often mix them up. In speech the imperfective извињавам се is more common, and извини and извините are simply «sorry» and «excuse me».

examples.en: Pick up your things and go!
Pick up your stuff and get lost!

examples.sr: Спаковала је све своје [пи̏нкле] и отишла.
examples.en: She packed all her belongings and left.
Kids, pick up your toys from the playground!

related.en: things — the neutral word
stuff, rags — colloquial, plural only
belongings, clothes — colloquial, plural only
belongings, junk — colloquial, plural only, often of children's toys

note: Ства̏ри is neutral; the other three are colloquial and used only in the plural.

examples.en: The child has started to walk.

related.en: to walk — the way of moving itself
to go on foot — a long way, or instead of transport
to stroll, to take a walk — aimless, for pleasure

note: «To go to school» is ићи у школу: хо́дати describes only the act of walking.

related.en: flowers (in general) — collective: plants or a bouquet
blossoms, individual flowers — countable, on a plant

note: Цве̑ће is a singular neuter noun: it has no plural.

examples.en: There they are on the table.

related.en: here is — an object near the speaker
here is — an object near the listener; «here he is» when someone was awaited
there is, over there — far from both

note: With a pronoun the short form is used: е̏во га, е̏то га, е̏но га.

examples.en: I arrived a little before you.

related.en: just now — one word: a recent moment in the past
a little earlier — a comparison in time, usually with something

note: After ма̏ло пре̏ comes the genitive: ма̏ло пре̏ по́дне, ма̏ло пре̏ те̏бе.

examples.sr: [И̏ако] је био уморан, наставио је да ради.
examples.en: Although he was tired, he kept working.

examples.sr: [И а̏ко] буде падала киша, ићи ћемо.
examples.en: Even if it rains, we'll go.

related.en: although — a concessive conjunction, written as one word
even if — «и» plus the conditional «ако», written as two words

note: И̏ако can be replaced by ма̏да: ма̏да је би̏о у̏мо̄ран.

examples.en: He learned the poem by heart.

related.en: by heart — an adverb, written as one word
to mind, into one's head — a preposition plus a noun

note:
Set expressions:
• па̏сти на па̏ме̄т, до́ћи на па̏ме̄т - «to come to mind»
• зна̏ти на̏паме̄т - «to know by heart»

related.en: afternoon — a noun, one word
after noon — an expression of time, two words

note: A synonym of the adverb is попо́дне: до́ћи ћу попо́дне - «I'll come in the afternoon».

examples.en: Clothes are cheap in this store.
I found an apartment at a good price.
Prices in small shops are affordable.

related.en: cheap — simply a low price, sometimes hinting at quality
favorable, good-value — the price is right and the terms are good
affordable — a price a person can afford

note: The opposite is ску̑п («expensive»).

examples.en: I'm late because there's a traffic jam.

related.en: because — a causal conjunction; can be replaced by «зато што»
question particle — a colloquial form of «је ли»

note: They cannot be swapped. You often hear јел тако? - «isn't that so?»

examples.en: Send me a picture from the wedding.

related.en: picture, painting, photo — the broad word
photograph — a picture taken with a camera

note: Every фотогра̀фија is a сли̏ка, but not the other way round. «To take a photo of» is сли̏кати or фотогра̀фисати: сликај ме - «take my picture».

examples.en: Paying money into the account is free.
Salary is paid on the fifth of the month.

related.en: payment in, deposit — money is put in
payment out, payout — money is handed out: salary, pension

note: The verbs are у̀платити and испла́тити. «To withdraw money from an account» is по̀дићи но̀вац.

examples.en: I hung a picture on the wall.
They fell out for no reason.
Don't pick a fight with him.

related.en: to hang up — to hang or attach on purpose: a picture, a poster
to hang, to hook — also: to snag, to catch an illness, to pick a quarrel

note: Зака̏чити фа̑јл - «to attach a file». In the sense «to hang» the two verbs are almost interchangeable, and ока̏чити has no other meanings.

related.en: her, hers (possessive) — changes with gender and number: «њена књига»
her (full accusative form) — after a preposition, at the start of a phrase, for emphasis
her (short accusative form) — the usual unstressed clitic, in second position
her (clitic before «је») — replaces «је» next to the auxiliary «је»

note: «To her» (dat.): the short form is јој, the full form њо̑ј.

meanings: немој, не смеш, не мораш or не треба?

examples.sr: [Не̏мојте] бринути, све ће бити у реду.
examples.en: Don't worry, everything will be fine.
You don't have to pay right away.

examples.sr: [Не тре́ба] да купујеш хлеб, имамо га.
examples.en: You don't need to buy bread, we have some.

related.en: don't — a direct prohibition or request; «немојте» is the polite form and the plural
you must not, you're not allowed — a taboo, a rule, the law
you don't have to — you may skip it
no need to — there is no point or necessity

note: As in English, «must not» and «don't have to» differ: не мо̑ра̄ш - «you don't have to», не сме̑ш - «you must not».

meanings: смејати се, насмејати се, осмехнути се or смешити се?

examples.en: The kids are laughing loudly in the yard.

examples.sr: Сви су се [на̀смејали] кад је испричао виц.
examples.en: Everyone burst out laughing when he told the joke.
She just smiled and walked past.
He has been smiling mysteriously all day.

related.en: to laugh — loudly and for a long time
to burst out laughing — the start of laughter, a reaction to a joke
to smile (once) — quickly, without a sound
to smile (for a while) — to keep a smile on one's face

note: Nouns: сме̑х - «laughter», о̏сме̄х - «smile».

examples.en: Put the book on the table.
Put the bag down on the floor.

related.en: to put, to place, to put on — the universal verb
to lower, to put down — downward movement
to pass (an exam), to lay — formal

note: Поло̀жити has the imperfective пола́гати: пола́гати ѝспит - «to take an exam».

examples.en: Tell him to wait for me.
I need to book a doctor's appointment.

related.en: to order (goods, a service) — the main verb for ordering: food, shoes online
to tell, to send word, to entrust — «поручи му да...»
to recommend — to suggest a film, a restaurant, a book
to schedule, to book — an appointment, a meeting

note: A table is reserved like this: резѐрвисати сто̑.

examples.sr: Не [мо̀гу] да отворим прозор, заглављен је.
examples.en: I can't open the window, it's stuck.

examples.sr: Нико није [смѐо] да јој каже истину.
examples.en: Nobody dared to tell her the truth.

related.en: to be allowed, to dare — permission, rules, etiquette, courage
can, to be able to — physical possibility, ability

note: In a polite request both work: могу ли да седнем? and смем ли да седнем? The difference is clear in the negative: не сме̑м - «I'm not allowed», не мо̀гу - «I can't (it doesn't work)».

examples.en: The dog is man's best friend.
Give this meat to your doggie.

related.en: dog — the neutral word
dog, cur — colloquial, sometimes derogatory
doggie — a child's, affectionate word
doggie, pup — affectionate, also of an adult dog

note: A puppy is штѐне. Ку̏чка is a «bitch», with a rude shade.

meanings: близу, недалеко од, поред or око?

examples.en: The house is near the school.
The hotel is not far from the center.
The pharmacy is next to the post office.
The children are running around the table.

related.en: near, close (+ gen.): «близу школе»
not far from — almost the same as «близу»; «од» is required
next to, beside — right next to: «поред прозора»
around; about — around something or approximately: «око стола», «око сат времена»

note: Поред тога - «besides that, in addition».

examples.en: I have enough time for work.
I have quite a lot of time.

related.en: enough (for a purpose) — whether there is enough for something: «имам довољно времена»
a lot, quite a lot; enough — quantity

note: Compare: до̏ста до̀бро - «quite good», до̏во̄љно до̀бро - «good enough» for the job.

examples.sr: Управо сам [схва̀тио] где сам оставио кључеве.
examples.en: I just realized where I left my keys.

related.en: to understand — a process: a deep understanding of a language, logic, feelings
to grasp, to realize — in a moment, a sudden realization; perfective

note: Схва̏тити also means «to take, to perceive»: схва̏тити о̏збӣљно - «to take seriously».

examples.en: A man walked into the post office.

related.en: «I am» (from «бити») / alone, by oneself — an auxiliary verb and an adjective
only, just — an adverb, does not change
one; a, a certain — a numeral and an indefinite «some»: «једна», «једно»

note: Сам occurs twice: in урадио сам то сам the first is «I am», the second «myself».

examples.sr: [Шта̏ го̏д] да се деси, остани миран.

related.en: anyone, anything, any — it does not matter which
whoever, whatever — a concession or a generalization

note: Било goes before the question word: било где, било како. Го̏д goes after: где̏ го̏д, кад год.

related.en: question particle «ли» — always two words in questions
gave — the plural past of «дати»

note: A question can also be asked without да ли: долазиш ли сутра?
